# ChapGTP, ILLC's Attempt at Raising a BabyLM: Improving Data Efficiency by Automatic Task Formation

**Jumelet, Langedijk, Hanna, Pouw, de Heer Kloots & van der Wal — "ChapGTP, ILLC's Attempt at Raising a BabyLM: Improving Data Efficiency by Automatic Task Formation"** · arXiv:2310.11282 (v1) · serialisation: the native arXiv HTML, converted with page marks against the arXiv PDF (task-008, 2026-08).

**An external work; the abstract is given.** The subject of the paper is a report on taking part in the BabyLM challenge (training a language model in a low-resource setting). Grokking is one of the strategies that did not make it into the final model; what the corpus values here is a negative point on language data. Set aside by the triage of task-021 (2026-08-26). No work of the corpus cites it yet. The introduction and the quoted paragraphs are translated lazily, as quotations appear (decision D2-b). The original — [`original/`](original/2310.11282.chapgtp-illcs-attempt-at-raising-a-babylm-improving-data-efficiency-by-automatic-task-formation.md); the analysis of the claims is the neighbouring `…claims.txt`.

# Abstract

*"We present the submission of the ILLC at the University of Amsterdam to the BabyLM challenge (Warstadt et al. 2023), in the strict-small track. Our final model, ChapGTP, is a masked language model that was trained for 200 epochs, aided by a novel data augmentation technique called Automatic Task Formation. We discuss in detail the performance of this model on the three evaluation suites: BLiMP, (Super)GLUE, and MSGS. Furthermore, we present a wide range of methods that were ultimately not included in the model, but may serve as inspiration for training LMs in low-resource settings."*
